pass_a_gloss: …and you will tread upon basilisk. Verse 10. But indeed behold beasts beside you. Of the same. Beside you, Job, beside everyone mindful (given to remembrance), beside everyone who has conquered. Verse 10. Grass equally with oxen he eats. He says the worms, the ones from him eating him down. For end, he says, my hand by you; and behold as grass he devours. Verse 11. And his power on navel of belly. This the first power against the man. To make a fornicator it begins from here. Of the same. In order that he signify the female, in order that he show that it campaigns not only against those having the seeds. And very most fittingly he named loin in the case of a male, and navel of belly in the case of a woman: and behold the strength, his loin in strength; and his power on navel of belly. Verse 25. And nations of Phoenicians share it out. Since Canaanites are slandered (accused) with great wickedness, who are also Phoenicians; through this he says: and nations of Phoenicians will divide him. Each one takes some part from the dragon, if he be the race Canaanite and Phoenician. Verse 20. And every floating thing having come together, they will not carry one hide of his tail. The last things of the dragon and the extreme things all floating things together are not able to make dead. The human beings, using the bodies as boats, are not able to carry one hide of his tail. They themselves by themselves are not able; but divine power overseeing, we are able not only one hide of his tail, but also the whole of him to carry, and the whole of him to make dead. And we make dead each one, so much as is upon himself, the devil, according to what was said by the Apostle: And the God may crush the Satan under your feet in quickness. Chapter 41, verse 4. Who will uncover the face of his clothing? Through what did he not say: who will uncover his face? What does also the clothing do here? For who will uncover, he says, face of his clothing? In order that the thing said be understood, let us use an example of the masks being put around, and not appearing this which they are, but they wish to seem. For they take up masks, bring to say (for example)…
pass_b_english: … and on the basilisk you will tread (Psalm 91:13).
“But see, there are wild beasts beside you” (Job 40:15).
From the same: Beside you, Job; beside everyone who is mindful; beside everyone who has won the victory.

“He eats grass just like oxen” (Job 40:15). He means the worms, the ones that came out of Job himself and were eating him up. For “an end,” he says, “my hand by you”; and see, it eats him up like grass.
“And his power is on the navel of his belly” (Job 40:16). This is the first power set against the man. It is from here that it begins to make him a fornicator.

From the same: This is said to signify the female, to show that it wages war not only against those who carry the seed. And most fittingly of all, he named the loin in the case of the male and the navel of the belly in the case of the woman: “See, his strength: his loin is in strength; and his power is on the navel of his belly” (Job 40:16).

“And nations of Phoenicians divide it up” (Job 41:6). Since the Canaanites, who are also the Phoenicians, are charged with great wickedness, that is why he says, “And nations of Phoenicians will divide him up.” Each one takes some part of the dragon, if by race he is a Canaanite and a Phoenician.

“And if every ship came together, they could not carry a single hide of his tail” (Job 41:7). The last parts of the dragon, his very extremities, all the ships together cannot put to death. Human beings, who use their bodies as ships, cannot carry a single hide of his tail. By themselves, on their own, they cannot. But when divine power watches over us, we are able to carry not only a single hide of his tail but the whole of him, and to put the whole of him to death. And each of us puts the devil to death, as far as it lies with himself, in keeping with what is said by the Apostle: “And may God crush Satan under your feet soon” (Romans 16:20).

“Who will uncover the face of his clothing?” (Job 41:13). Why did he not say, “Who will uncover his face?” What is the clothing doing here as well? For “who will uncover,” he says, “the face of his clothing?” So that what is said may be understood, let us use the example of the masks that people put on, who do not appear as what they are but as what they wish to seem. For they take up masks, let us say, …

choices.choice: 'Τοῦ αὐτοῦ' rendered as the lead-in 'From the same:' at the head of each note; no authorship guessed beyond it.
'Τοὺς σκώληκας λέγει' is 'He means the worms' (the speaker of the verse), not 'Origen hears the worms'.
Catena stichos labels (ιʹ, ιαʹ, κεʹ, κʹ; ΚΕΦ. ΜΑʹ δʹ) are not printed; each lemma carries its KJV verse by its words. LXX/MT 40:30-31 = KJV 41:6-7; LXX/MT 41:5 = KJV 41:13.
'Συντέλεια γὰρ, φησὶ, τὴν χεῖρά μου ὑπὸ σοῦ' has no verb; translated word for word and flagged, no sense supplied.
Opens with '…' (Psalm 91:13 quotation continues from u03-rem-close) and ends with '…' (sentence continues in u04-rem-early).
